audit.why: 41.94% over 62 games — one of the worst in this slice, and the sides say why: Gragas owns 3-5 and both item stages, Aurora holds only level 1 and the level-6 stage. Barrel Roll is 850 range on a 10s cooldown and Drunken Rage reduces the damage he takes on a 5s cycle, so he wins nearly every trade you can start.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and gave no cooldown for Explosive Cask, which is the ability the content layer correctly identifies as the lane-decider.
audit.why: Explosive Cask is 100/85/70 seconds against Between Worlds' 140/120/100 — he gets his back 40 seconds sooner at rank 1, so the page's own advice to 'only commit when his E and R are both down' has to be read against a 100-second clock, not an even trade.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) is your commit. Explosive Cask is only 100s and knocks you out of your own rift — wait it out.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and mid both call the level-6 play an 'untargetable window' and an 'untargetable all-in'. Aurora has no untargetability. The underlying point they are making — that Explosive Cask displaces you out of your own rift — is correct and much better without the false premise. Separately, Drunken Rage's damage reduction is missing from both layers.
audit.why: Riot's Drunken Rage (W, 5s): 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing, he becomes boisterous and belligerent, dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received.' The one-second sample is a visible tell and the damage reduction is what eats your burst — so bursting into a fresh Drunken Rage is the single most common way this lane is lost, and it is on a 5-second cycle so you cannot wait it out; you have to burst in the gap right after his empowered auto lands. Barrel Roll (Q, 10/9/8/7/6, 850) 'explodes on its own after 4 seconds. The potency of the explosion increases over time' — so a cask he lets sit is much stronger than one he detonates instantly, which is why standing near a placed cask is worse the longer you do it. Happy Hour (P) heals him on every skill cast, which is what anti-heal answers.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage reduces damage he takes for 5s — burst in the gap after his empowered auto, not into the sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is tracked as the matchup-defining cooldown with no number.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 and is his engage and stun; Barrel Roll is 10s; Drunken Rage is 5s and never meaningfully down. Body Slam is the only one whose downtime creates a window.
audit.corrected: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 — that downtime is your only walk-up window.

audit.why: breakdown.late already carries anti-heal as core, which is right: Happy Hour heals him on every skill use, so his sustain scales with how often he casts, not with how well he trades.

But at 6 his R flips it back: the Explosive Cask knockback interrupts your W commit and can punt you clean out of your own rift, so the zone converts nothing while his ult plus a Drunken Rage auto out-trades you. notes: Drunken Rage's damage reduction is the reason this lane sits at 41.94% and it appears nowhere on the page. It is on a 5-second cycle, so it cannot be waited out — the only real answer is to burst in the window immediately after his empowered basic attack resolves. Barrel Roll's potency also increases the longer the cask sits, which makes standing near a placed cask progressively worse rather than a fixed risk; neither layer says so.
